title: Console Route Experiments — Wireframes Review Notes (Creation Flow + Results Dashboard)
content:
Attendees
- Design: Tessa Morgan (lead), Kenji Nakamura (workflow), Alicia Perez (metrics/results)
- Product: Marissa Cole
- Eng (Console & Tooling): Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin, Felix Schneider
- Eng (Routing/Policy): Jada Williams (context for precedence + stop semantics)
- Observability/Telemetry: Logan Wright, Allison Grant
- Auth/RBAC: Kaitlyn Nguyen

Meeting context
- Review of early wireframes for the Route-level A/B testing framework in Console.
- Focus areas: (1) experiment creation wizard (route selection → variants → traffic split → guardrails → review), (2) results dashboard & drilldowns.
- Goal: identify usability gaps, missing guardrails, and “gotchas” for beta customers; converge on next iteration for DES-311 / DES-322 and unblock ENG-9025 implementation.


1) High-level feedback (what’s working)
Creation flow
- The “Create experiment” entry point under Rollouts is discoverable and matches customer mental model (treat experiments as an operational control, not purely analytics).
- Route selection step makes it clear experiments are “per route” (vs global). Good alignment with routing/policy constraints.
- Variant cards are easy to scan; the “variant name + model version + optional notes” layout will help support/on-call.

Results dashboard
- Side-by-side variant comparison concept is strong: baseline vs challenger(s) is more readable than a long list.
- The “Guardrail status banner” at top is the right pattern; consistent with other Rollouts safety surfacing.
- Proposed tabs (Overview / Latency / Cost / Errors / Quality) map well to our measurement hooks and avoid a single overstuffed view.


2) Creation wizard review notes
2.1 Step 1 — Route selection
What we saw
- Wireframe shows route dropdown/search + basic route metadata (endpoint name, environment, last deploy, current model).

Feedback
- Need “route identifier normalization” clarity: users should see the friendly name AND the canonical route id used in metrics.
  - Suggest: primary label = route name; secondary = route_id (copyable).
- Add a lightweight warning state if route has unusually high cardinality path patterns (e.g., raw paths) that may impact results readability.
- Add explicit environment scoping in UI (prod/staging) to reduce “why don’t I see traffic?” confusion.

Open questions
- Do we allow multi-route experiments in v1? (current wireframe implies single route)
  - Product leaning: single route in beta/GA to limit blast radius and simplify attribution.

Action items
- Kenji: add route_id secondary label + copy icon; add environment selector/label.
- Dylan/Chloe: confirm API can return route metadata needed for the selector (route display name, env, current policy).


2.2 Step 2 — Variants configuration
What we saw
- Variants include: variant name, description, model selection, optional “advanced” toggles.

Feedback
- Model selection needs compatibility guidance:
  - If a chosen model is incompatible with the route’s schema/tooling requirements (e.g., tool calling / structured output), we should fail early with actionable text.
  - Prefer “inline validation” (blocking) rather than only at final review.
- Baseline concept: the UI should clearly indicate which variant is “control/baseline” (used for deltas).
  - Proposed: first variant defaults to “Baseline” and cannot be removed unless another is promoted.
- Naming guidance: customers tend to use “A/B”, but internal debugging benefits from semantic names.
  - Suggest UI helper text: “Use short names like ‘llama3.1-70b-q4’ or ‘mixtral-8x7b-v2’.”

Unresolved UX question
- How to expose “variant headers” behavior (assigned variant returned to client) without scaring customers?
  - Support feedback from other features: users misinterpret debug headers as a required integration step.
  - Recommendation: default show assigned variant in Console only; in API responses, show headers but label as optional troubleshooting.

Action items
- Alicia/Tessa: define baseline labeling pattern for the variant cards and comparison charts.
- Felix: confirm what we can display from results API (baseline_id vs inferred) for deltas.
- Marissa: align copy with docs plan (avoid implying customers must read headers).


2.3 Step 3 — Traffic split editor
What we saw
- Slider / percentage inputs for split across variants.

Feedback
- Precision vs speed: include both slider and numeric input. Slider alone makes it hard to set 1%/5% safely.
- Pre-set ramp templates would reduce friction and increase safety:
  - Suggested quick actions: “Start at 1%”, “5%”, “10%”, “50/50”, “Even split”.
- Add clear blast-radius language:
  - “Traffic split applies to eligible requests on this route only” plus link to eligibility rules.

Open questions
- Do we allow changing split while running? (likely yes)
  - Needs audit logging + change history surfaced; also potential “cooldown” warning (metrics need time to stabilize).

Action items
- Kenji: add quick-action split templates + numeric inputs.
- Chloe: confirm update-split API semantics + whether split changes are immediate vs propagated (and how we show “in progress”).


2.4 Step 4 — Eligibility + stickiness key
What we saw
- Eligibility appears as a simplified set of conditions (tenant/account filters, headers, region), plus stickiness configuration.

Feedback
- Biggest risk area: “stickiness key” selection and missing identifiers.
  - The UI must explain default precedence and what happens when keys are absent.
  - Need proactive warning when a chosen key is likely low-entropy (e.g., constant header or empty), which can cause skew.
- Recommend a “Test assignment” tool during creation:
  - Input: sample request headers/account id/user id (depending on what they have).
  - Output: assigned variant + hash inputs used.
  - This is both UX and support/on-call tool; aligns with internal debug endpoint effort.

Unresolved UX question
- What is the “default stickiness key” in GA?
  - Proposal discussed: prefer customer-provided stable key if present (e.g., x-redwood-sticky-key) else fall back to customer_id/account_id; last resort randomized per request (with warning).
  - Need to avoid silent fallback to low-entropy values.

Action items
- Tessa + Kaitlyn: draft UX text for stickiness defaults and warnings.
- Dylan/Jada: confirm feasible “test assignment” flow (can call internal debug endpoint behind RBAC).


2.5 Step 5 — Guardrails configuration
What we saw
- Guardrails step includes thresholds for latency/error/cost and optional “quality regression” toggle.

Feedback
- Defaults need to be very explicit and conservative.
  - Proposed baseline: p95 latency regression threshold + error rate delta threshold + cost/token delta threshold.
  - If we’re doing soft-stop by default, the UI should say “will notify and mark experiment degraded; optionally can auto-stop” (if enabled).
- Clarify what metrics are evaluated on:
  - Window length (e.g., last 10 minutes / last hour), minimum sample size, and whether it’s per-region or global.
- Quality guardrails:
  - Make it clear quality metrics may be delayed and sampled.
  - Avoid presenting “quality” as definitive; use language like “eval score (sampled)”.

Open questions
- How to present soft-stop vs hard-stop without confusing users?
  - Proposal: two-tier toggle
    - Default: “Notify + mark degraded” (soft)
    - Advanced (behind feature flag or admin-only): “Auto-stop on severe regression” (hard) with kill switch.

Action items
- Alicia: propose guardrail UI layout that emphasizes defaults + “advanced” section.
- Marissa + Dylan: confirm what we can commit to for beta vs GA (auto-stop availability, kill switch).


2.6 Review + Confirm screen
Feedback
- Add explicit summary of:
  - Route(s), eligibility, stickiness key, variant models, split, guardrails, expected propagation/staleness window.
- Add “permissions check” early:
  - If RBAC will block start/stop, show that before user invests time configuring.

Action items
- Felix: add “RBAC preflight” design note (how to surface permission errors gracefully).


3) Results dashboard review notes
3.1 Overview tab
What we saw
- KPI tiles + small charts showing deltas and current split.

Feedback
- Make “current traffic split” + “assignment health” prominent.
  - Add a small “Assignment integrity” tile:
    - attribution drop rate
    - % requests missing stickiness key
    - variant 0 traffic detection (if any variant receiving ~0)
- Add “Propagation status” indicator:
  - Show config version + last updated time + estimated propagation lag.
  - Helps explain stale/partial results tickets.

Action items
- Alicia: add assignment integrity + propagation status to overview.
- Logan/Allison: confirm which integrity metrics are available for Console (and what sampling caveats exist).


3.2 Latency tab
Feedback
- Users want p50/p95/p99 on the same chart, but we need to avoid clutter.
  - Recommendation: default p95 chart with selector for p50/p99.
- Include region filter (but guard against cardinality explosion):
  - Allow selecting from top 5 regions by traffic for the experiment.

Unresolved question
- Are latency metrics computed at request-level only, or token-level too?
  - If both exist, UI should label clearly (“request latency” vs “time to first token” vs “per-token latency”).

Action items
- Chloe/Felix: confirm metric naming + availability from results API.


3.3 Cost tab
Feedback
- Cost needs both “total cost” and “unit economics” (cost per 1k tokens or cost/token).
- Define what “cost” means (GPU + platform? effective blended?)
  - Add tooltip with our canonical definition.

Action items
- Nadia/Logan (follow-up outside this meeting): provide tooltip text + confirm which cost fields are stable for beta.


3.4 Errors tab
Feedback
- Separate “HTTP errors” vs “model errors” if possible.
- Add a “top errors” table with a link to traces/logs (for internal users) and a generic description for customers.

Action items
- Felix: propose table layout and what’s feasible given data sources.


3.5 Quality tab (eval score integration)
Feedback
- Label clearly as “Sampled eval score” with the prompt set name.
- Must show confidence caveat: “Not enough samples yet” state.
- Add a “What is this?” drawer linking to docs on evals.

Action items
- Olivia Grant / Jonas Weber: provide example output + recommended aggregation window.
- Alicia: create empty state designs for low-sample scenarios.


3.6 Change history / Audit trail
Feedback
- The “Change history” should appear in the experiment detail view as a tab, not buried.
- Each entry should show: actor, timestamp, change summary (split change, guardrail change, start/stop), and “view diff”.
- Customers asked about export: we should reference audit export capability (if enabled) and retention.

Action items
- Felix + Kaitlyn: ensure UI and backend align on “diff summary” shape; identify redaction rules.


4) Navigation + terminology consistency
Feedback
- Decide on naming in UI:
  - “Route experiments” vs “Experiments” vs “A/B tests”
  - Strong recommendation (Design): UI label “Experiments” with helper text “Route-level A/B testing” to avoid jargon overload.
- In results, avoid calling variants “treatments” (too stats-y). Stick to “Variant”.

Action item
- Tessa/Marissa: finalize glossary for UI and docs.


5) Known implementation constraints called out by Eng/Obs
- Cardinality concerns: avoid allowing arbitrary dimensions (model_id x region x route_id) displayed simultaneously. Start with safe defaults and curated filters.
- Attribution drop rate is a top risk; we need to show a health signal so customers don’t misread missing data as “variant wins/loses.”
- Propagation lag/staleness: results dashboard should display freshness so support doesn’t chase phantom regressions.


6) Decisions made in this review (tentative)
- Single-route experiments for beta/GA (no multi-route in wizard for now).
- Baseline variant must be explicitly marked; UI should default first variant as baseline.
- Traffic split editor will include numeric inputs + ramp templates.
- Results Overview will include “Assignment integrity” and “Propagation status” indicators.
- Quality tab will be clearly labeled as sampled + can show “not enough samples” states.


7) Follow-ups / owner list (consolidated)
Design
- Kenji: update route selection + traffic split templates + numeric inputs; incorporate stickiness warnings placeholder.
- Alicia: redesign results Overview with integrity + propagation; propose guardrail layout emphasizing safe defaults; define baseline comparison visual language.
- Tessa: draft stickiness key copy + finalize terminology glossary.

Engineering
- Chloe: confirm API semantics for split updates + propagation status; confirm metric naming & availability (latency/cost/errors).
- Felix: confirm baseline id support in results API; propose audit trail UI/diff shape; implement RBAC preflight UX handling.
- Dylan/Jada: feasibility for “test assignment” tool using internal debug endpoint behind RBAC.

Telemetry/Obs
- Logan/Allison: confirm which integrity metrics are feasible for Console (drop rate, missing sticky key rate, variant 0 traffic, staleness).

Product
- Marissa: confirm beta vs GA commitments for auto-stop; align header messaging with docs/support expectations.


Notes to self (Design)
- Biggest risk of UX failure is not the charts; it’s users not understanding assignment/stickiness and then distrusting results.
- We should bias toward explicit warnings + “health of data” indicators in beta, even if it makes the UI feel slightly more operational.

Next review
- Schedule 30-min follow-up once revised wireframes are ready (target: week of 2025-03-03) focusing on stickiness/test assignment UX + guardrail step copy.
